_comment: Pointers that do not resolve and are not defects. The gate blocks GROWTH of
this list, not its existence: adding an entry is a deliberate act with a
reason, removing one is free. `why` is not read by the gate — it is read by
the next person deciding whether the entry still earns its place.
Three kinds live here, and only three should. (1) A path in SOMEBODY ELSE'S
tree, cited as evidence — the gate cannot fetch it and a citation is not a
claim about our repo. (2) A path the doc says DOES NOT EXIST — a forward
reference to a file still to be authored, or a wrong pointer quoted as the
defect under discussion. (3) A module a design doc PROPOSES.
A path that is simply stale does not belong here. Fix it.

unresolved.why: Third party — KittyCAD Modeling App's own tree, quoted as prior art for pick-a-face-to-source.
Third party — Monaco's published dist layout, cited for a measured bundle size.
Third party — SWC's published config schema, cited for what it does *not* cover.
Quoted defect. The doc reproduces a wrong pointer bikar's gate caught (real file: packages/core/src/graph/face-extractor.ts). Repairing it would delete the evidence.
Deliberately nonexistent — the injected path in that doc's mutation test of a pointer gate.
Third party — a page fetched during the survey, cited for what it fails to state.
Third party, and a recorded negative result: the doc says the ERROR/MISSING node documentation was **not found** there.
Third party, same recorded negative result.
Proposed module. Both mentions are conditional ('a kernel3d/split.ts that reuses them...'), and §Q3 has not decided whether it is built at all. Fix by building it or by settling Q3 the other way.
Third party — MachineBlocks' OpenSCAD source, cited for its calibration defaults.

Model to author — MC-8's in-situ gap ladder. Same shape as Text-Coupon.bkr below: CAL-CLR-01 names MC-8 as what settles it, so the entry exists before the file does. Nothing blocks writing it — the geometry is six wall pairs — it is unwritten because printing is user-held and an unprintable plate settles nothing. Remove this when the file is written.

Model to author — MC-7 needs the `text` statement, which is T2 in docs/text-emit-design.md §8. The entry exists now because CAL-TXT-01/02 name MC-7 as their coupon, and a bet whose coupon is written down nowhere is the W-F1 defect. Same shape as LG-B2's grandfathered entry before its model landed. Remove this when the file is written.

Deliberately deleted. D-042 names this file as the thing it removed — a whole test file certifying the withdrawn centreline rule — and the D-034 note above it records the same removal. The path must stay exact for the record to be checkable; repairing it to something that resolves would be inventing a file that never comes back.
